newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Clabecq workers delay response to lay-offs.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Clabecq workers delay response to lay-offs.

text.p: Workers at bankrupt Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq SA, which was placed in receivership on Friday and will continue activities, are to decide on January 10 whether to resume work, Belgian media said on Saturday.
A Belgian commercial court declared loss-making Clabecq bankrupt on Friday and appointed four receivers to run the firm. Its order book is full for at least three months.

Clabecq's 1,800 workers are due to be sacked, and court-appointed experts had proposed that just over 1,300 be immediately re-employed on short term renewable contracts while the receivers sought a takeover candidate, the radio said.

Workers meeting on Saturday to consider their response to the court's ruling decided to reconvene next Friday when they would vote on whether to resume work having received notice of dismissal and knowing how many of them would be taken on again.
The socialist FGTB trade union told Saturday's meeting of Clabecq workers that it was opposed to all redundancies.

Belgium's Walloon Regional Government, Clabecq's majority shareholder and biggest creditor, has said it is prepared through its SWS steel investment arm to meet operating losses which arise from the continuation of activities at the firm.
"It think it will be important to maintain industrial activity...at Clabecq," Walloon Government President Robert Collignon told Belgian RTBF radio on Saturday.
Guaranteeing Clabecq's operating losses would "allow, in the bankruptcy scenario, the chances of finding a new industrial operator to be maximised", he added.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy in mid-December after the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc ($47 million) rescue plan by the Walloon Region which then withdrew its support for the firm.
The Commission's decision has been challenged by both Clabecq's unions and the regional government.
